# VeriFactu records (REC)

The billing record behind each invoice under VeriFactu: how it is generated, chained and sent to AEAT, and what to do with AEAT's answer.

Rules page: https://docs.beel.es/rules/records

"Checked by: Your integration" or "The issuing business" means BeeL. does not enforce the rule, beyond any error codes it lists: the integration has to.

## REC-001

**Each issued invoice gets a billing record built from its data**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

When an invoice is issued, its billing record (registro de alta) is generated at that moment from the invoice's own data: issuer, recipient, number, dates, type, description, totals, regime and the tax breakdown of each line. BeeL. generates it; you classify each line correctly.

**Why:** The record is what AEAT registers. A line classified wrongly on the invoice is registered wrongly too, and only a later document can change it.

**Applies to:** operations `issueCompanyInvoice`; Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 9 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a9
- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 10.1 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a10

**Incorrect:** Classifying an exempt line as a 0 % taxed line: AEAT registers a taxed operation.

**Correct:** Sending the exemption reason on the line, so the record carries the exempt base and its cause.

**Related:** REC-002, REC-004, LIF-001

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/compliance-and-responsibilities#what-beel-does-for-each-invoice · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/what-aeat-receives

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-001.md

## REC-002

**The record goes to AEAT as soon as the invoice is issued**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

Every billing record is sent to AEAT continuously and automatically, as the invoice is issued. BeeL. submits it without a call from you; issue each invoice when the operation happens rather than holding drafts to issue in batches.

**Why:** Under VERI*FACTU the immediacy of the submission is part of the record's security. There is no per-invoice switch and no later submit step.

**Applies to:** operations `issueCompanyInvoice`; Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 16.1 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a16
- AEAT, Preguntas frecuentes SIF y VERI*FACTU, Sistemas VERI*FACTU — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/iva/sistemas-informaticos-facturacion-verifactu/preguntas-frecuentes/sistemas-verifactu.html

**Incorrect:** Keeping a day's sales as drafts and issuing them all at midnight.

**Correct:** Issuing each invoice when the sale happens; BeeL. submits its record straight away.

**Related:** REC-001, REC-007, DAT-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/auto-submit

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-002.md

## REC-003

**VERI*FACTU is kept until the end of the year**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: medium · Checked by: The issuing business. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

Once a NIF has sent its first record under VERI*FACTU, it keeps that modality at least until 31 December of that year. Leaving it is declared in a submission before the year ends.

**Why:** The option is annual: switching a NIF off in the middle of the year breaks the obligation it took on with its first submission.

**Applies to:** A NIF that has started sending records under VERI*FACTU.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 16.5 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a16
- Orden HAC/1177/2024, art. 17.2 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22138#a17

**Incorrect:** Turning VeriFactu off for a NIF in June after it started submitting in March.

**Correct:** Deciding before year end whether the NIF continues next year.

**Related:** REC-002, DAT-011

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/compliance-and-responsibilities#verifactu-modality-only · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/enabling-verifactu

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-003.md

## REC-004

**BeeL. generates the hash and the chain**

`MUST NOT` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

Do not compute a hash or chain records yourself. Each record carries a hash and refers to the previous record of the same issuer; BeeL. generates both when the invoice is issued.

**Why:** The chain is what makes the records traceable from the first to the last. A second chain kept by your system would not be the one AEAT receives.

**Applies to:** Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 8.2.b) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a8
- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 12 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a12
- Orden HAC/1177/2024, art. 7.a) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22138#a7

**Incorrect:** Computing a SHA-256 over your own invoice fields and sending it with the invoice.

**Correct:** Issuing through BeeL. and reading verifactu.invoice_hash from the invoice if you need it.

**Related:** REC-001, REC-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/erp-integration#who-generates-the-record-the-hash-and-the-chain

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-004.md

## REC-005

**One chain per NIF, one company per NIF**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

Records of each taxpayer are kept apart, in a chain of their own. Create one company per NIF and issue each invoice from the company of the NIF that issues it; show your users which one they are operating.

**Why:** A system used by several taxpayers must keep their records separate and meet the requirements for each one; an invoice issued from the wrong company lands in another taxpayer's chain.

**Applies to:** Accounts that invoice for several NIFs.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 7.a) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a7
- Orden HAC/1177/2024, art. 7.c) — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22138#a7

**Incorrect:** Issuing the invoices of two businesses from one company, told apart by a series prefix.

**Correct:** Creating a company per NIF and targeting each call at the right one.

**Related:** REC-004, REC-011

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/multi-nif#the-model

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-005.md

## REC-006

**No certificate is needed to sign records**

`SHOULD` · Law · Impact: low · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

Records sent under VERI*FACTU need no electronic signature: their hash is enough. Neither the issuer nor the integrator hands BeeL. a digital certificate for the submissions.

**Why:** Integrations that plan a signing step, or ask their customers for a certificate, add work the regulation does not require.

**Applies to:** Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- RD 1007/2023 (RRSIF), art. 16.3 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2023-24840#a16

**Incorrect:** Asking each customer to upload a certificate so that their invoices can be signed.

**Correct:** Asking the NIF holder to sign the AEAT representation once, and nothing else.

**Related:** REC-011, REC-004

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/faq#do-i-need-a-digital-certificate · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/compliance-and-responsibilities#representation-not-a-certificate

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-006.md

## REC-007

**Keep invoicing when AEAT is unreachable**

`MUST NOT` · Law · Impact: medium · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

Do not stop invoicing because AEAT is unavailable. The invoice is issued and numbered as usual; BeeL. retries its submission on its own and flags a record that goes out on a later day than the issue date as a late submission.

**Why:** An incident in the submission never justifies stopping invoicing, and records have to be sent as soon as it is possible, in order and flagged as late.

**Applies to:** Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Legal basis:**

- Orden HAC/1177/2024, art. 16.4 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22138#a16
- AEAT, Preguntas frecuentes SIF y VERI*FACTU, Sistemas VERI*FACTU — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/iva/sistemas-informaticos-facturacion-verifactu/preguntas-frecuentes/sistemas-verifactu.html

**Incorrect:** Queueing sales in your system until AEAT is back, then issuing them with the day's date.

**Correct:** Issuing through BeeL. as usual and following each invoice with the verifactu.status.updated webhook.

**Related:** REC-002, REC-008, DAT-002

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/erp-integration#aeat-does-not-answer · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/what-aeat-receives#dates-and-late-submission

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-007.md

## REC-008

**Follow submission_status and fix what AEAT rejects**

`MUST` · BeeL. rule · Impact: critical · Checked by: Your integration. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

Track each issued invoice's verifactu.submission_status (NOT_SUBMITTED, PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED) through the verifactu.status.updated webhook and a periodic reconciliation. A REJECTED invoice is not registered: read its error_code and fix it.

**Why:** A 200 on issue means BeeL. accepted the invoice, not that AEAT registered it. A rejection nobody reads leaves an invoice outside AEAT's records.

**Applies to:** operations `getCompanyInvoice`, `listCompanyInvoiceVerifactuRecords`; Invoices of a company under VeriFactu.

**Incorrect:** Treating the 200 of the issue call as proof that AEAT registered the invoice.

**Correct:** Subscribing to verifactu.status.updated and, every few hours, listing invoices still NOT_SUBMITTED or PENDING to reconcile them.

**Related:** REC-009, REC-010, QRC-002

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/submission-states#the-fiscal-states · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/handling-rejections#reconcile-do-not-only-listen

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-008.md

## REC-009

**Check the data AEAT accepted with errors**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: Your integration. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

When AEAT accepts a record but reports an error (ACCEPTED with an error_code), check the data it flagged, usually the recipient's NIF and name. If it was wrong, issue a corrective invoice with the right data; if it was right, nothing else is needed.

**Why:** A record accepted with errors stays in AEAT with those errors until a later document fixes them.

**Applies to:** Invoices ACCEPTED with an error_code.

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 4.3.1 — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** Reading ACCEPTED and ignoring the error_code next to it.

**Correct:** Reading error_message, confirming the customer's NIF was mistyped, and issuing an R1 corrective with the right one.

**Related:** REC-008, COR-001

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/handling-rejections#accepted-with-errors

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-009.md

## REC-010

**Resubmission fixes only causes outside the invoice**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: medium · Checked by: Your integration. BeeL. does not check this; you must.

Resubmitting a record (subsanación) is only for a problem that needs no corrective invoice: a cause outside the invoice's data, such as an issuer not yet in the census or an unsigned representation. There is no API for it; once the cause is fixed, ask BeeL. support to resubmit. Any error in what the invoice says is fixed with a corrective.

**Why:** The record is immutable: resubmitting it does not change the invoice, so it cannot fix a wrong amount, customer or description.

**Applies to:** Records rejected or accepted with errors.

**Decides:**

- *Nothing on the invoice is wrong: AEAT refused the record for a cause outside it (issuer not in the census, representation not signed).* → Fix the cause, then ask BeeL. support to resubmit the unchanged record (subsanación).

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 4.3.1 — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** Asking support to resubmit an invoice whose recipient NIF was wrong.

**Correct:** Signing the missing representation, then asking support to resubmit the rejected record unchanged.

**Related:** REC-008, COR-001, VOI-001

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/handling-rejections#when-to-contact-support · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/cancel-and-fix

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-010.md

## REC-011

**The NIF holder signs the AEAT representation first**

`MUST` · Law · Impact: high · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. rejects a request that breaks it.

Before a NIF issues real invoices under VeriFactu, its holder signs the AEAT representation that lets BeeL. submit the records on the taxpayer's behalf. Enabling VeriFactu or issuing without it is rejected.

**Why:** Records are sent by the taxpayer or by someone acting as its representative. Without the signed representation there is nobody entitled to send them.

**Applies to:** operations `generateCompanyRepresentation`, `submitCompanyRepresentation`, `updateCompanyVeriFactuConfiguration`, `issueCompanyInvoice`; Production (Live) NIFs; sandbox needs no representation.

**Error codes:** [`VERIFACTU_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRED`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/VERIFACTU_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRED), [`NIF_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRED`](https://docs.beel.es/errors/NIF_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRED)

**Legal basis:**

- Orden HAC/1177/2024, art. 5 — https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2024-22138#a5

**Incorrect:** Enabling VeriFactu in Live for a new NIF straight after creating it: the API answers VERIFACTU_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRED.

**Correct:** Generating the representation document, having the holder sign it, uploading it, and then enabling VeriFactu.

**Related:** REC-006, REC-005

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/compliance-and-responsibilities#representation-not-a-certificate · https://docs.beel.es/verifactu/enabling-verifactu#sign-the-aeat-representation

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-011.md

## REC-012

**Tax amounts are base times rate**

`MUST` · AEAT criterion · Impact: low · Checked by: BeeL. API. BeeL. does this for you.

The tax amount of each breakdown equals its base times its rate, with the same sign as the base. BeeL. computes it from the rate of each line: the API takes rates, never tax amounts.

**Why:** AEAT checks the tax amount against base × rate, allowing 10 € of difference, and rejects the record beyond it.

**Applies to:** Every taxed line.

**Legal basis:**

- AEAT, Validaciones y errores VERI*FACTU (v1.2.2), 3.1.3.15.7 CuotaRepercutida — https://www.agenciatributaria.es/static_files/AEAT_Desarrolladores/EEDD/IVA/VERI-FACTU/Validaciones_Errores_Veri-Factu.pdf

**Incorrect:** Keeping a tax amount computed by your system and expecting BeeL. to register it.

**Correct:** Sending the rate on each line (main_tax) and reading the computed amounts from the response.

**Related:** REC-001, TAX-001

**Explained in:** https://docs.beel.es/guides/amounts-and-rounding#taxes-are-rounded-per-group-not-per-line

**Full rule, with the legal text quoted:** https://docs.beel.es/rules/REC-012.md
